Bootstrap of scaling positions

Source: R/svt.R
scboot.Rd

Standard errors and percentile intervals of Aldrich-McKelvey stimulus positions (amscal()) or Basic Space weights (bbscal(), first dimension, of the matrix or of its transpose) by resampling respondents with replacement (Efron and Tibshirani 1993). Draws come from seed, as set.seed() takes it. The sign of a Basic Space dimension is arbitrary, so its replicates are best compared after aligning them.

Usage

scboot(Z, method = "am", nboot = 200, seed = 42)

Arguments

Z

A respondent-by-stimulus (or issue) matrix, NA for missing.

method

"am", "blackbox" or "blackbox_t".

nboot

The replicates; nboot times the positions (rows and columns of Z) must be at most 67108864 (2^26).

seed

The seed.

Value

A list of class scboot: se, mean, lo, hi (2.5% and 97.5%) and nboot.

References

Efron, B. and Tibshirani, R. J. (1993). An Introduction to the Bootstrap. Chapman & Hall.

See also

Other scaling: amscal(), anchv(), anomin(), bamscl(), bbscal(), bmdsf(), bunfld(), cjrirt(), cmdsf(), cutlns(), dblctr(), dwnom(), dynirt(), indscl(), ipsrec(), irtem(), irtlik(), irtpst(), mdsfit(), mlsmu(), nmdsf(), nombt(), nomll(), nompr(), nomutl(), nrmvec(), optcls(), ordirt(), ordocl(), procrs(), smacf(), smunf(), unfstr(), votagr(), wrdfsh()

Examples

set.seed(1)
Z <- matrix(rnorm(100), 20, 5) + rep(1:5, each = 20)
scboot(Z, nboot = 10)$se
#> [1] 0.09685089 0.13563335 0.07232775 0.09721725 0.07797385
